memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not resort to divination as at other times, but turned his face toward the wilderness. When Balaam looked out and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came on him. - Num 24:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something shifts in Balaam here. After two failed attempts to secure a curse, he finally stops resorting to sorcery and simply turns to look at Israel spread out before him. The tricks and techniques are set aside. And in that moment, the Spirit of God comes upon him.

Notice what Balaam sees: Israel encamped tribe by tribe, ordered and settled under God's care. What Balak intended as a scene to be cursed, God transformed into a sight of beauty and blessing. The very people the king feared were, in God's eyes, a people wonderfully arranged and protected.

There is a lesson in Balaam's turning from divination. All his attempts to manipulate the outcome had come to nothing. Only when he abandoned his schemes and looked plainly at what God was doing did the truth come through. Sometimes we too must lay down our efforts to control and simply behold what God is doing.

We cannot manufacture God's blessing through techniques or formulas. His Spirit moves according to His own purpose. For those in Christ, we are given the Spirit not as a reward for our cleverness but as a gift of grace (Gal 3:2). Lay aside every attempt to manipulate God, and simply look to what He is doing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever try to manipulate outcomes rather than trusting God?
2. What might change if you laid down your schemes and beheld God's work?
3. How does God transform what others see as ordinary into something blessed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me lay aside my attempts to control and simply behold what You are doing. Fill me with Your Spirit, given by grace, and let me trust Your good purposes. Amen.
